title: Probe localization — 7q22.1
clinical_history: Place an educational locus probe on the chromosome 7 map at the address already used for band practice. The probe is a teaching definition, not a commercial assay and not a disease marker. Demonstration ideogram.

probe_type_expected.detects: presence or copy number of one locus
probe_type_expected.normal_pattern: two red signals, one on each chromosome 7

hints: 7q22.1 is on the long arm of chromosome 7.
Numbering increases from the centromere toward the telomere. The sub-band .1 is the slice of 7q22 closest to the centromere.
A locus-specific probe marks one address. A centromeric probe marks copy number of a whole chromosome.
explanation: The probe is stored at chromosome 7, arm q, band 22, sub-band 1, matching segment 7q22.1 in the chromosome map. This exercise reuses that address. It does not introduce a disease locus.
plain_language_interpretation: The red probe belongs at 7q22.1 on the chromosome 7 ideogram.

references.label: ISCN
references.citation: McGowan-Jordan J, Hastings RJ, Moore S, eds. ISCN 2020. Basel: Karger; 2020. Band designation.
